clue.text: Risk using railway on the way to London destination

parts.note: to risk something is to chance it
a lane is a way or narrow road

explanation.surface: A gambler hops on a train heading into London.
explanation.walkthrough: Chancery Lane is a street and Underground station in central London, home to the legal profession.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancery Lane is a street and Tube stop in central London, so a place a traveller there might be heading.

clue.text: Will addition land detectives back in a bind?

indicators.note: to land something in a place is to put it there, so this works with 'in' to set one piece inside another
taken with 'land', this places the turned detectives inside the word for a bind

parts.note: a coil is a binding loop, something that binds

indicators.note: back tells us the detectives' abbreviation is read in reverse order

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives

explanation.surface: A question of whether police can be dragged into a tangle over a will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' is a verb here, to set something down, working with 'in'; 'back' turns the detectives round. CID is the UK police Criminal Investigation Department.
explanation.definitionFit: A codicil is a supplement appended to a will after it was first made.

clue.text: Criminal activity of a third-born child

indicators.note: third here picks only the third letter of the following word born

parts.note: a son is a male child

explanation.surface: An offence committed by the third child to be born in a family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third-born' looks like one idea, a child's birth order, but 'third' takes the third letter of 'born', R.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a crime.

clue.text: Garden — short one, where gale is raging

parts.note: curt means short or brusque
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: raging suggests wild, tossed-about motion, so the word gale is scrambled

explanation.surface: A small garden somewhere battered by a howling storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raging' rearranges GALE into LAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtilage is the enclosed land, such as a yard or garden, attached to a house.

clue.text: Downfall of former countess Spencer reported

indicators.note: reported means the name is spoken, so we want a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Raine, Countess Spencer, was Princess Diana's stepmother

explanation.surface: Gossip pages tracking the fall from grace of an aristocratic stepmother.
explanation.walkthrough: Raine Spencer, a well-known British society figure, was stepmother to Princess Diana; her first name sounds like the weather word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain is water falling from the sky, a literal fall downwards.

clue.text: Supporter will watch over cricketer's pad

parts.note: a leg supports the body or a table
to guard is to watch over

explanation.surface: A backer promises to look after a sportsman's protective padding.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman straps padded guards to the legs to protect them from the hard ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg guard is the padded shin protection a batsman wears.

clue.text: At no time in French city except Sabbath

indicators.note: except means leaving out, so the Sabbath's letter is removed from the city

parts.note: Nevers is a city in central France

explanation.surface: A French town where something never happens, except on the day of rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Never means on no occasion whatsoever.

clue.text: Iron hook used to set off sparkler

indicators.note: set off can mean to arrange or rearrange, so the letters of iron and hook are reordered

explanation.surface: A metal hook being used to light a firework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sparkler' suggests a firework but means a diamond; 'set off' rearranges IRON HOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: The Koh-i-Noor is a famous diamond in the British Crown Jewels, and a gem is slangily a sparkler.

clue.text: Servant boy fetched firewood

parts.note: in old British boarding schools a fag was a junior boy who served an older pupil
fetched means got, as in went and got

explanation.surface: A young servant went off and brought back firewood.
explanation.walkthrough: A fag was a younger pupil acting as servant to a senior at an English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Faggot is an old word for a bundle of sticks tied together for burning.

clue.text: Leaving Sahara after carol is beheaded

indicators.note: after puts the desert piece in front, with the carol piece following it

parts.note: the Sahara is the largest hot desert

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is cut off the word for carol

parts.note: to carol is to sing

explanation.surface: Someone walking out of the desert after a carol singer has lost his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is beheaded' removes the S from SING, leaving ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserting means abandoning or going away from a person or post.

clue.text: Play on this flower-girl

definitions.meaning: something one plays, a stringed instrument of the violin family
a violet-type plant that is also a girl's name

explanation.surface: Instructions for a girl selling flowers in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A viola is both a bowed instrument slightly bigger than a violin and a pansy-type bloom, as well as a woman's name.

clue.text: Frank can't quite finish Voltaire's novel

indicators.note: can't quite finish means the last letter of the novel's title is dropped

parts.note: Candide is Voltaire's satirical novel of 1759

explanation.surface: A man named Frank struggles to get to the end of a French classic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a reader's name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means honest and outspoken, straightforward.

clue.text: Grooming in Indian cooking

definitions.meaning: rubbing down and combing a horse
preparing food in a spicy sauce from the subcontinent

explanation.surface: A line about getting ready while preparing a South Asian meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To curry a horse is to brush it with a currycomb, and currying food is cooking it as a spiced dish.

clue.text: Rope found while negotiating a trail

indicators.note: negotiating suggests working one's way round obstacles, so the letters of a trail are reworked

explanation.surface: A rope turns up as someone makes their way along a path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiating' rearranges A TRAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a lasso, a long noosed rope used by cowboys.

clue.text: Held back by employer?

definitions.meaning: kept back or kept hold of
engaged or kept on by an employer, as a lawyer is on a fee

explanation.surface: A worker kept behind by the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Retained means kept, and a barrister or adviser is retained when hired on a retainer fee.

clue.text: Escape when magistrate isn't in — he has right to imprison

indicators.note: to imprison is to shut inside, so one piece goes within the magistrate's word

parts.note: beak is British slang for a magistrate or judge
someone who isn't in is out

explanation.surface: A prisoner flees while the magistrate who could lock him up is away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beak' is old British slang for a magistrate; R goes inside it to give BREAK.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakout is a jailbreak, a getaway from confinement.

clue.text: A first-rate chap getting in a state

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word rate

parts.note: a gent is a man or chap
taken as written

explanation.surface: A top-notch fellow becoming agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first-rate' reads as excellent but splits: 'first' takes R from 'rate'; 'in a state' looks like agitation, but 'state' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a country in South America, and a state can mean a nation.

clue.text: Trees in their colourful settings?

parts.note: imagines a grove of trees whose surroundings are painted a single bright hue, crimson forests

explanation.surface: Wondering about trees seen against bright autumn backdrops.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer describes forests of a particular colour; together it names giant Californian conifers.
explanation.definitionFit: Redwoods are huge sequoia trees, and the split reading gives crimson forests as their setting.

clue.text: Understood the gun he used was revolutionary

parts.note: gat is old American slang for a gun
red is a common term for a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A gangster grasped that his gun had a spinning chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests a revolver's spin but gives RED, a radical.
explanation.definitionFit: To have gathered something is to have inferred or grasped it.

clue.text: Man who started major riots

parts.note: points to the eighteenth-century Protestant lord whose surname was given to the anti-Catholic disturbances of 1780 in London

explanation.surface: Asking who instigated a great civil disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord George Gordon led the 1780 protest that became the Gordon Riots, the worst disorder in London's history.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord George Gordon's agitation sparked the London riots that bear his name.

clue.text: One must be fly to spot this fungus as poisonous!

definitions.text: One must be fly to spot this fungus as poisonous!

parts.words: One must be fly to spot this fungus as poisonous!
parts.note: fly means sharp or alert, but the toxic red-capped toadstool is itself called the fly variety

explanation.surface: Warning that only a sharp-eyed forager can tell a toadstool is toxic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' is British slang for shrewd; the fly agaric is the red, white-spotted poisonous mushroom, so the fungus must be 'fly' to be the toxic kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Agaric is a gilled mushroom, and the fly variety is the classic poisonous toadstool.

clue.text: Old iron basket with family emblem round outer side

indicators.note: round means the emblem goes around another piece placed within it

parts.note: a crest is the heraldic emblem of a family

indicators.note: outer takes only the first and last letters of the word side

explanation.surface: An antique metal holder decorated with a coat of arms around its edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outer side' gives S and E, the first and last letters of 'side', which go inside CREST.
explanation.definitionFit: A cresset was a metal cage or cup on a pole holding burning fuel as a torch or beacon.

clue.text: Natural effects when 4 bends

parts.note: the number points to the solution of 4 Down
to bow is to bend

explanation.surface: Phenomena that appear when a certain weather pattern curves.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' is a cross-reference: put in the answer to 4 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: These arcs of colour are optical phenomena of nature caused by sunlight in droplets.

clue.text: Slow down when reaching thicket

definitions.meaning: reduce speed, as a driver does
a dense patch of undergrowth or bracken

explanation.surface: A driver easing off on coming to dense woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: To brake is to decelerate a vehicle, and a brake is also an old word for scrubby undergrowth.

clue.text: When in a frenzy, men produce such protein

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words frenzy and men

explanation.surface: Excited males generating some biological substance.
explanation.definitionFit: An enzyme is a biological catalyst, a type of protein that speeds up reactions in the body.

clue.text: A brute to take Gulliver's name!

definitions.meaning: the label the travelling hero hears for the bestial humans in the land of the horses

explanation.surface: Taking on the name of Swift's hero would make one a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: In Swift's Gulliver's Travels the Yahoos are degraded humanlike creatures, and the horses take Gulliver for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo is an uncouth person, from the brutish creatures in Swift's satire.

clue.text: Knock out in return — mad!

indicators.note: in return signals the word for mad is read backwards

parts.note: nuts means crazy or mad

explanation.surface: Retaliating with a furious punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' reverses NUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to knock someone senseless.

clue.text: Love to get a great letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
mega is slang for great or huge

explanation.surface: A loved one receiving a wonderful note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' suggests correspondence but means a character of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: When these birds itch, sores develop

indicators.note: develop suggests one thing turning into another, so the letters of itch and sores are rearranged

explanation.surface: Flightless birds getting sores whenever they scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develop' rearranges ITCH SORES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostriches are large flightless African birds.

clue.text: Behaving stupidly when eating together — a fight ensues

parts.note: to mess is to eat communally, as in a military mess
a bout is a boxing or wrestling fight

explanation.surface: Diners in a canteen act like fools until a brawl breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' is the military word for eating meals together.
explanation.definitionFit: Messing about means fooling around, acting in a silly way.
